findings.title: Rescheduling bookings bypasses deferred email cancellation and deletes booking before reminder cleanup finishes
findings.body:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, rescheduling calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` inside an unawaited `forEach` loop right before `await eventManager.reschedule(...)`. There are two issues here:
1. Passing `immediateDelete = true` immediately sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` to SendGrid rather than setting `cancelled: true` on the `WorkflowReminder` record for the cron job to process within 1 hour of the send time. This defeats the purpose of the PR for rescheduled bookings and will still contribute to hitting SendGrid's 100 pending `scheduled_sends` limit.
2. `eventManager.reschedule` deletes the `originalRescheduledBooking` row from the database. Because `WorkflowReminder.booking` has `onDelete: Cascade` in `schema.prisma`, deleting the original booking cascades and deletes its `WorkflowReminder` rows. If `immediateDelete` were `false`, cascading deletion would wipe out the `WorkflowReminder` rows before the cron job (`scheduleEmailReminders`) ever runs to cancel them in SendGrid; and with unawaited async calls in `forEach`, it also races with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`.

findings.title: `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders`
findings.body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called on line 19, but `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is never called on the `@sendgrid/client` instance (unlike in `emailReminderManager.ts` line 26). When the cron endpoint runs in a serverless function or process where `emailReminderManager.ts` has not been imported, `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` (line 57) and `client.request({ url: "/v3/mail/batch", ... })` (line 188) will fail with 401 Unauthorized from SendGrid, preventing scheduled emails from being cancelled or batch-scheduled.

findings.title: Single SendGrid failure in cancellation loop aborts all deletions, including already-cancelled reminders
findings.body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (lines 53-77), each `client.request` to SendGrid is awaited inside the `for` loop, while the corresponding `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are pushed into `workflowRemindersToDelete` and only executed at `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop finishes (Note: Prisma's `.delete()` is a `PrismaPromise` that only executes when awaited/then'd). If cancelling the Nth reminder throws an error (for example, if `referenceId` is missing or SendGrid returns an error for one batch ID), control jumps to the `catch` block: the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped, and none of the first N-1 reminders that were already cancelled in SendGrid are deleted from the database, causing them to be re-processed on the next cron run.

findings.title: Paid booking cancellations return early before cancelling workflow reminders or scheduled jobs
findings.body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, when `bookingToDelete.paid` is truthy (lines 363-465), the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking as `REJECTED`, and returns on line 464. Because the code that cancels `scheduledJobs` and `workflowReminders` is located further down at lines 480-493, cancelling a paid booking never cancels its scheduled workflow email or SMS reminders (nor its Zapier scheduled jobs), so reminders will still be sent for cancelled paid bookings.

findings.title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` races with `workflowStep.delete` cascade
findings.body: In `workflows.tsx` (lines 518-531) and in `delete` (lines 212-225), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` are invoked inside a synchronous `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)` (or `workflow.deleteMany`). Because `WorkflowReminder.workflowStep` has `onDelete: Cascade` in `schema.prisma`, deleting the workflow or step cascades and deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows in Postgres while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` / `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` are still awaiting network calls to Twilio/SendGrid, causing their subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls to fail with `P2025` (record not found), and risking unfinished external API calls if the serverless execution finishes as soon as the mutation returns.

findings.title: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with `immediateDelete` leaves orphaned `WorkflowReminder` row in DB
findings.body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts` lines 213-223), when `immediateDelete` is true, it sends the cancel request to SendGrid and immediately returns without deleting the `workflowReminder` record from the database (or marking it cancelled). If the caller does not cascade-delete the parent workflow/step, the `WorkflowReminder` row remains in the database with `cancelled: null`.
